# Incident Report: Koi Stealer Infection — 2024-09-04

## Evidence reviewed
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,091 frames, capture spans DHCP lease at t=0 through ~3,576s)
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` / `.jpg` (Suricata/ET/GPL alert export)

## Victim host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.17.0.99** |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** (confirmed via ARP: `172.17.0.99 is at 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4`, and matches eth.src on all traffic from this IP) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (DHCP option 12 hostname; corroborated by NBNS `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>`/`<20>` and DNS registration `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.bepositive.com`) |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** (Kerberos `CNameString` in AS/TGS exchanges between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller) |

LAN context: domain is `bepositive.com`, domain controller/DNS server is **172.17.0.17** (NBNS `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19`, MAC `00:23:ae:50:ba:fd`), default gateway is **172.17.0.1** (MAC `00:02:4b:51:8c:b6`). The SMB/Kerberos alerts against 172.17.0.17 (`ET INFO SMBv1 in use`, `GPL NETBIOS SMB Session Setup NTMLSSP...overflow attempt`, `GPL RPC kerberos principal name overflow`) are normal domain-authentication (SMB IPC$/Kerberos TGT) traffic from the workstation to its DC that trip generic lightweight IDS rules — benign context, not exploitation.

## Malware family

**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer). Attribution is **signature-confirmed**: the alert export contains `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits) fired directly against the POST traffic from 172.17.0.99 to 79.124.78.197:80, alongside `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser 1` (50 hits) on the same stream. This is independently corroborated by the packet contents: the malware POSTs a pipe-delimited beacon (`<len>|<bot-GUID>|<session-id>|<base64 blob>`) to a bare-IP host with no accompanying DNS lookup, using a static, outdated spoofed User-Agent — all classic Koi Stealer C2 checkin behavior.

Example decoded beacon body (frame 1668, TCP stream 48):
```
101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=
```
The GUID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` is the persistent bot ID used across the beaconing session.

Delivery vector: not observed. The capture begins at DHCP lease acquisition and the first C2 POST occurs only ~7 minutes in; no executable/document download precedes it over HTTP in this capture, so the infection either predates this capture or arrived via a channel not visible here (e.g., an earlier session, removable media, or an encrypted download). Note: a TLS connection to `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201) closes only ~2.6 seconds before the first C2 beacon — flagged as a possible staging/loader connection, but its content is TLS-encrypted and cannot be confirmed as part of the delivery chain.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `79.124.78.197:80/tcp` — Koi Stealer C2 server. 96 beacon POSTs to `/foots.php` between 2024-09-04 21:35:07 and 22:31:55 (local capture time, UTC+4), plus a gate exchange on `/index.php`.

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — repeated stealer data exfil/checkin (Content-Type: application/octet-stream, spoofed IE7 User-Agent)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — C2 gate/registration GET, server responded with gate token `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — POST (encrypted/binary payload, 105 bytes)

**Malicious IP**
- `79.124.78.197` — no DNS resolution observed for this host anywhere in the capture; contacted directly by bare IP (matches the "Suspicious POST to Dotted Quad" alert).

**Domains**
- No malicious domain was observed — the C2 uses a bare IP, not a hostname. `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201) is noted above as a temporally-adjacent but unconfirmed context indicator, not a confirmed IOC.

**Files / hashes**
- None available. The `/foots.php` and `/index.php` HTTP responses to the beacons carry no body content (chunked, zero-length), and no executable or document object was transferred over HTTP in this capture. No SHA256 can be computed from this evidence.

**Malware artifact identifiers (host-side, for hunting)**
- Bot/victim GUID: `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`
- Beaconing User-Agent: `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)`

## Benign context (ruled out, not indicators)
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` GET `/assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` — legitimate Adobe update-check telemetry (uses a similar legacy IE-style UA by design; response is a 4-byte plaintext status, not stealer traffic).
- `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `*.msn.com`, `*.microsoft.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `x1.c.lencr.org`, `sso.godaddy.com` — standard Windows/Office/Edge OS telemetry and connectivity checks.
- SMB/Kerberos traffic to DC 172.17.0.17 — normal domain-joined authentication, not lateral movement (the GPL alerts on this traffic are rule false-positives on legitimate NTLMSSP/Kerberos protocol fields).
